subject: blobfish
title: The Blobfish Isn't a Blob. We Only See It After It's Destroyed

scenes.text: The world's ugliest animal doesn't actually look like that.
Blobfish live 600 to 1,200 meters down, off Australia and New Zealand.
Down there, they look like a normal fish: big head, tapered body, like a tadpole.
They have no swim bladder and loose, jelly-like flesh, held in shape by the crushing pressure.
Haul one up in a net, and the pressure drops so fast its body collapses and sags.
So the famous face is what decompression damage looks like.

description:
The blobfish only looks like a blob after it is dragged up from 600 to 1,200 meters deep.
In its home water it looks like an ordinary tadpole-shaped fish; with no swim bladder and soft flesh, its body collapses when the pressure drops on the way up.
Should the blobfish lose its title of world's ugliest animal?
first_comment: Now you know the blobfish's secret. Which deep-sea animal should we look at next?
